# Trigger phrases: what to say to invoke each sprezzature-* skill

**Generated by `scripts/build_triggers.py`** from every shipped skill's `SKILL.md` description. **Do not hand-edit.** A test in `tests/test_triggers_md.py` asserts this file equals the generated output on every commit. To change a phrase, edit the relevant `SKILL.md` and re-run the generator.

The trigger phrases below are what each skill's frontmatter description claims will activate it in Claude Code / OpenCode. They are not the only phrases that work (the agent matches prompts to the description holistically), but they are the ones the maintainer guarantees.

## Route on what the user is holding

A phrase list cannot generalise: the ways to ask for a chart, a colour or a caption are unbounded, and a user almost never names the tool. What IS bounded is the kind of thing they have in front of them. Match that first; the phrase table below is confirmation, not the mechanism.

| What the user is holding | Skill | Said without naming a tool |
|---|---|---|
| A screen to build: a page, a component, a form, a dashboard | **sprezzature-ui** | "build me a settings page", "I need a modal", "scaffold a landing page", "audit this UI", « une page pour… » |
| A command-line tool somebody who will not type it needs to run | **sprezzature-cli-gui** | "my colleague keeps getting the flags wrong", "can non-technical people use this", « une interface pour l'équipe » |
| Markdown that has to become a site somebody else can find | **sprezzature-publish** | "put this online", "why does this look bad when shared", "SEO", "favicons", "make it readable for a wider audience" |
| HTML — usually HTML YOU JUST WROTE, before anyone asks; An image that needs words: alt text, a description, a caption | **sprezzature-accessibility** | "is this accessible", "missing alt", "unlabelled input", « vérifie l'accessibilité »; "describe this image", "draft alt text", "this img has no alt" |
| A colour being chosen or judged — any colour, in any context | **sprezzature-colors** | "what colour should this be", "does this pass contrast", "is this colour-blind safe", « quelle couleur pour ce fond » |
| Recorded speech somebody needs as text, a question about that text — or written text somebody needs as speech | **sprezzature-audio** | "what did they say in this meeting", "who spoke when", "subtitles", "read this aloud", « de quoi ils parlent dans cet enregistrement » |
| An interface somebody is complaining about the FEEL of | **sprezzature-ux-laws** | "this page is overwhelming", "too many options", "I can never find the button", « c'est confus » |
| Numbers you want somebody to SEE — or a picture of a chart that is hard to read | **sprezzature-figures** | "show me this data", "which region is biggest", "what does this look like", "a colleague sent me this graph", « fais-moi voir », « un visuel de ça » |
| Numbers attached to PLACES — a column of countries, regions, states, départements | **sprezzature-maps** | "which countries are worst affected", "break this down by region", "where is this happening", "who holds the east", « par département » |
| A video that states a fact about a project — or a project that changed under a film already shipped | **sprezzature-video** | "make a launch video", "the demo video is out of date", "is this number still right", "re-cut the film", « refais la vidéo » |

Two of these fire on work you just did rather than on a request: **sprezzature-accessibility** on any HTML you authored, and **sprezzature-ux-laws** on any interface you authored. Waiting to be asked means the markup nobody checked is the markup you wrote.

Several can be right at once. A page you just built is a **ui** job, then an **accessibility** lint, a **ux-laws** audit and a **colors** contrast check — three different questions about one artefact, and passing one says nothing about the others.

## When NOT to fire

The phrase table only ever argues for firing. Ten siblings compete for every prompt, and the clause that argues *against* one is what keeps a contrast question away from the a11y linter and a hex map away from the cartographer. Each skill carries its own, in the same `description` an agent reads to choose — not only here.

| Skill | Not this one when |
|---|---|
| **sprezzature-ui** | the thing to wrap is a command-line tool (sprezzature-cli-gui); the source is Markdown that must become a site (sprezzature-publish); or the HTML exists already and the question is whether it is accessible (sprezzature-accessibility), how it feels (sprezzature-ux-laws) or whether a colour passes (sprezzature-colors). The exhaustive trigger catalogue is in `references/triggers.md`. |
| **sprezzature-cli-gui** | the screen has no CLI behind it (sprezzature-ui). The exhaustive trigger catalogue is in `references/triggers.md`. |
| **sprezzature-publish** | the page is built and the question is accessibility (sprezzature-accessibility), or the speech is recorded and needs transcribing rather than generating (sprezzature-audio). The exhaustive trigger catalogue is in `references/triggers.md`. |
| **sprezzature-accessibility** | the question is contrast or colour-blindness (sprezzature-colors), captions for speech (sprezzature-audio), or how the interface feels (sprezzature-ux-laws). NOT a replacement for axe-core / Pa11y / Lighthouse. The exhaustive trigger catalogue is in `references/triggers.md`. |
| **sprezzature-colors** | the markup has structural defects rather than a colour question (sprezzature-accessibility), or the colours belong to a chart being drawn (sprezzature-figures). The exhaustive trigger catalogue is in `references/triggers.md`. |
| **sprezzature-audio** | the job is to wire a narration into a page — player, read-along highlighting, the site (sprezzature-publish, which calls this one for the voice) — or the words describe an image (sprezzature-accessibility). The catalogue is in `references/triggers.md`. |
| **sprezzature-ux-laws** | the defect is mechanical accessibility (sprezzature-accessibility), contrast (sprezzature-colors), or the screen has yet to be built (sprezzature-ui). The exhaustive trigger catalogue is in `references/triggers.md`. |
| **sprezzature-figures** | the numbers are attached to real PLACES (sprezzature-maps). The exhaustive trigger catalogue is in `references/triggers.md`. |
| **sprezzature-maps** | the shape is schematic rather than geographic (hex map, spike map, binned grid, dot density over an outline), which live in sprezzature-figures. The exhaustive trigger catalogue is in `references/triggers.md`. |
| **sprezzature-video** | the ask is motion design, which belongs to the renderer. The exhaustive trigger catalogue is in `references/triggers.md`. |

## How discovery works

Claude Code / OpenCode read every installed skill's `SKILL.md` frontmatter at conversation start. When the user's prompt matches a description, that skill is loaded and its instructions become available. The agent matches semantically: phrases above are illustrative, not exhaustive. Say what you mean; the right skill should fire.

## Adding a new trigger

1. Edit the relevant `<skill>/SKILL.md` `description` field; add the new quoted phrase to the existing Trigger-phrase list.
2. Re-run `python scripts/build_triggers.py`.
3. Commit both files together; the test will refuse a commit where they drift.
